_comment: WrinkleFE validation ledger — machine-readable companion to VALIDATION.md.
Each case carries the full AnalysisConfig recipe (the 'harness reference
configuration'), the measured experimental knockdown, and a pinned
expected_analytical_kd computed by the current code. The pinned values are
REGRESSION BASELINES, not claims of experimental agreement: scripts/validate.py
recomputes them and fails if they move beyond rel_tolerance, which is the
reproducible-harness precondition named in issue #254 (and the revert of
00584b4) for re-landing the graded compression decay fix. Re-pin deliberately
with 'python scripts/validate.py --update' after an intentional model change.
STIFFNESS (issue #326): cases that also carry expected_analytical_modulus_kd
pin the closed-form CLT axial-modulus knockdown (analytical_modulus_knockdown,
added in #324) the same way; measured_kd_modulus is the matching experimental
stiffness knockdown, stored for reference only. The modulus baseline is UD-
scoped (1.0 for non-unidirectional layups), so it is pinned on the UD datasets
F (Li 2025) and G (Hsiao & Daniel 1996) only.
NOTE: the 'KD analytical' column published in VALIDATION.md for Li (2025) was
produced by an uncommitted script whose configuration could not be reproduced
from a clean checkout — exactly the gap this ledger closes going forward.
Elhajjar (2025), Mukhopadhyay (2015) and Li (2026) case-level data are not in
the repository (see README 'Validation'); add their datasets here when the
raw points land (tracked by issue #22's follow-ups).

datasets.name: li_2025_multi_wrinkle_compression
datasets.reference: Li, Li, Ge & Liang (2025), Polymer Composites 46(16):15176-15187, DOI 10.1002/pc.30121
datasets.status: included — strength via the calibrated penetration gate (GATE_LI2025_VACBAG, issue #161 resolved; the plain Budiansky-Fleck column is retained as the angle-only floor for drift detection). See VALIDATION.md.
datasets.width_convention: config width = wavelength (Gaussian 1/e length of one period)

cases.note: S-M-2 geometry at a near-surface interface (z = 10/14 through the thickness, carried as z_frac). The plain-BF strength and modulus predictions are identical to S-M-2 by construction; the penetration gate applies its through-thickness position factor P(z) (item D.5, calibrated to this single case), so expected_gate_kd reproduces the measured near-surface mildness.

datasets.name: hsiao_daniel_1996_ud_carbon
datasets.reference: Hsiao & Daniel (1996), Composites Science and Technology 56(5):581-593
datasets.status: active — UD carbon (IM6G/3501-6); the first dataset carrying a measured stiffness knockdown (issue #326). See VALIDATION.md 'Dataset G'.
datasets.amplitude_convention: config amplitude = crest height A (= half of peak-to-peak); amplitude_p2p_mm = 2A. theta_peak = arctan(2 pi A / lambda).
datasets.width_convention: config width = wavelength (matches the Li 2025 dataset recipe in scripts/validate.py case_config).
datasets.modulus_source: Hsiao & Daniel (1996) measured axial-modulus knockdown (uniform 0.571, graded 0.941); strength knockdown 0.660 for the graded specimen (VALIDATION.md Dataset G).

cases.note: Uniform-waviness coupon (A = 1.19 mm, lambda = 27.9 mm, 20 plies, t_ply = 0.95 mm, theta ~ 15 deg). Hsiao & Daniel report a measured MODULUS knockdown only (0.571); no measured strength knockdown for the uniform coupon, so measured_kd is omitted and expected_analytical_kd is a pure regression baseline. The shipped graded-Gaussian modulus path (width = lambda, mid-plane decay) is pinned here, not the periodic-RVE linear-taper estimate in validation/validate_modulus.py.

Graded-waviness coupon (A = 0.29 mm, lambda = 14.5 mm, 24 plies, t_ply = 0.381 mm, theta ~ 7.2 deg). Measured strength knockdown 0.660, measured modulus knockdown 0.941. expected_analytical_kd is the CURRENT code's graded profile-proportional Budiansky-Fleck output for this recipe (0.5127); the issue's indicative 'BF ~ 0.716' uses a textbook gamma_Y rather than the package's confinement-weighted gamma_Y_eff = 0.032 for [0]_24, so it is not the pinned value.

datasets.name: shi_2025_ud_cfrp_compression
datasets.status: active - Dataset H (UD half). First carbon strength dataset with an amplitude sweep at fixed span (t/T = 0.1-0.3, peak angles 12-33 deg). Plain Budiansky-Fleck pinned; no penetration-gate preset is calibrated for this material yet. See VALIDATION.md 'Dataset H'.
datasets.reference: Shi, Yang, Sun, Zheng, Qian, Wang & Song (2025), Materials 18:4503, DOI 10.3390/ma18194503 (CC BY 4.0)
datasets.amplitude_convention: config amplitude = trough depth t (the paper's wrinkle amplitude, one-sided surface dip); amplitude_p2p_mm = 2t only to fit the shared schema (config amplitude = amplitude_p2p_mm / 2).
datasets.width_convention: wavelength_mm = 2 x the paper's wrinkle span L = 5.5 mm (the span is the half-wave trough); width_mm = L/2-scale Gaussian envelope isolating the single trough.
datasets.geometry_note: One-sided wrinkle: trough depth t at the TOP surface decaying to a flat bottom over roughly the lower half of the laminate (paper Figs. 3 and 8). Modelled as morphology='tool_flat' with the flat tool face on the bottom and a 10-ply ramp: a uniform-amplitude CREST over the upper plies. For these symmetric layups the flat-bottom crest is the z-mirror of the paper's flat-bottom dip, and the mirror is a symmetry of the specimen, so the response is equivalent; the unmeasured decay shape (sketched only) is the real modelling assumption. Surface resin pockets are disabled: the bottom ply is exactly flat on the tool (zero gap) and the top surface follows the wrinkle in the specimens. Specimens 140 x 12 mm, ASTM D6641 clamped; the t/T = 30% failures involve buckling participation (stated in the paper), which a first-ply strength path cannot capture.

cases.note: t = 0.38 mm (t/T = 10%); mean ultimate load 25.2 kN of 39.5 kN pristine (paper Sec. 6).
t = 1.14 mm (t/T = 30%); mean 15.8 kN; buckling participation in the failures.

datasets.recipe_note: Ledger (analytical) recipe: plain graded profile at the default mid interfaces - the analytical path reads only the wrinkle PROFILE (peak angle), not the through-thickness decay, so the one-sided tool_flat representation is not needed here and is FE-only by design (its surface pockets are mesh physics). The FE scoring recipe in validation/strength_error_summary.py uses morphology='tool_flat' with the flat face on the bottom and a 10-ply ramp; see geometry_note.

datasets.name: calvo_2023_md_cfrp_tension
datasets.reference: Calvo, Quinonero-Moya, Feito, Miguelez et al. (2023), Composite Structures 323:117498, DOI 10.1016/j.compstruct.2023.117498
datasets.status: active - Dataset I. First TENSION strength set since B/C, first distributed multi-wave case, and the first experimental exercise of WrinkleFE's multi-wrinkle composition. Batch means (B5 with waves vs B4 without); effectively one strength point. See VALIDATION.md 'Dataset I'.
datasets.amplitude_convention: config amplitude = wave height delta (paper Fig. 2) = 0.5 mm; amplitude_p2p_mm = 2*delta only to fit the shared schema.
datasets.width_convention: wavelength_mm = 2 x the single-bump length; width_mm = half the bump length (Gaussian envelope isolating one bump per wave).
datasets.geometry_note: Seven transverse-strip waves at 17.5/27.5/.../77.5% of the 200 mm specimen (20 mm pitch), centre wave 2 plies below the top and the others 7, 13, 18 plies below it moving outward symmetrically (paper Sec. 2.1). The paper's three wave numbers are mutually inconsistent for a sinusoidal bump: lambda = 9.6 +/- 1 mm and delta = 0.5 mm give a 9.3 deg peak tangent, but the measured inclination is theta = 6.8 +/- 1.3 deg. The recipe keeps the measured height and matches the measured angle (bump length 13.2 mm), because the peak angle is what the analytical models consume; matching via delta = 0.366 instead gives the same analytical KD within 0.4 %. The literal 9.6/0.5 reading (9.3 deg) gives 0.613 - a documented sensitivity, not the recipe. Decay toward the tool side is unmeasured: graded with floor 0.5 (the wave persists toward the bag side); FE retention spans 0.45-0.62 over floors 0.25-0.75 at the literal geometry.

cases.note: Batch means: B5 (7 waves) 930 MPa vs B4 (no waves) 1106 MPa (paper Table 3). measured_kd_modulus is the INITIAL apparent modulus ratio 76.2/76.8; the end-of-test ratio (after off-axis ply cracking) is 64.3/71.0 = 0.906. Calvo's own CLT-with-waviness model predicts strength KD 815/1268 = 0.643 and modulus 0.916 initial.

progressive_damage._comment: Crack-band progressive-damage FE predictions, pinned so they stop drifting silently. These were previously only in untracked validation/li_progressive_*.csv artefacts; between 2026-07-04 and 2026-09-29 they moved by up to 0.034 per case with nothing to catch it. Unlike the analytical cases above, these numbers are MESH- AND Gf-LOCKED: the calibration is only valid at the recipe recorded per mesh below, and refining the mesh changes the answer materially (that is the point of the nx=36 entry, which is evidence, not a second calibration). Recompute with validation/validate_li_progressive.py.
progressive_damage.reference: Li, Li, Ge & Liang (2025), Polymer Composites 46(16):15176-15187, DOI 10.1002/pc.30121
progressive_damage._tolerance_comment: Looser than the analytical ledger's 1e-3: a load-stepping Newton solve to peak load is not bit-reproducible across BLAS versions the way a closed-form knockdown is. 2 % is tight enough to have caught the 0.034 (3.7 %) drift that motivated this section.

recipes.name: nx16_calibrated
recipes.role: calibration point — the mesh Gf was fitted at

recipes.name: nx36_refined
recipes.role: mesh-sensitivity sentinel — NOT a calibration. Pinned so the documented finding that refinement changes the answer cannot silently stop being true. One case only, to keep the slow lane affordable.
